subject: ddca
title: Unsigned binary
prompt: What decimal value does the unsigned binary number 101101₂ represent?
source: VisCon authored practice · not an ETH exam
explanation: The set bits contribute 32 + 8 + 4 + 1 = 45.

subject: ddca
title: Two’s complement range
prompt: What is the representable range of an 8-bit two’s complement integer?
source: VisCon authored practice · not an ETH exam
explanation: An n-bit two’s complement integer ranges from −2^(n−1) to 2^(n−1)−1.

subject: ddca
title: Two’s complement decoding
prompt: What decimal integer does 11111100₂ represent in 8-bit two’s complement?
source: VisCon authored practice · not an ETH exam
explanation: The unsigned value is 252; with the sign bit set, subtract 256 to get −4.

subject: ddca
title: A NAND output
prompt: For inputs A = 1 and B = 1, what does a two-input NAND gate output?
source: VisCon authored practice · not an ETH exam
explanation: NAND negates AND. Since 1 AND 1 is 1, its negation is 0.

subject: ddca
title: An XOR condition
prompt: A two-input XOR gate outputs 1 exactly when what holds?
source: VisCon authored practice · not an ETH exam
explanation: Exclusive OR is true for (0,1) and (1,0), but false for equal inputs.

subject: ddca
title: A multiplexer select
prompt: How many select bits does a standard 8-to-1 multiplexer need?
source: VisCon authored practice · not an ETH exam
explanation: Three bits encode 2³ = 8 possible inputs.

subject: ddca
title: A full-adder carry
prompt: A full adder receives A = 1, B = 1 and carry-in = 1. What are its sum bit and carry-out?
source: VisCon authored practice · not an ETH exam
explanation: 1 + 1 + 1 = 3 = 11₂: the low bit is the sum and the high bit is carry-out.

subject: ddca
title: A decoder’s outputs
prompt: How many outputs does a standard binary 3-to-8 decoder have?
source: VisCon authored practice · not an ETH exam
explanation: Three binary input bits select one of eight outputs.

subject: ddca
title: Edge-triggered storage
prompt: When does a positive-edge-triggered D flip-flop sample its D input?

options.text: Continuously while the clock is high

source: VisCon authored practice · not an ETH exam
explanation: An edge-triggered flip-flop samples at its designated clock edge, subject to timing requirements.

subject: ddca
title: Setup time
prompt: What does a flip-flop’s setup-time requirement specify?

options.text: How long Q must be high
How many instructions a processor executes
How long D must be stable after the edge only
How long D must be stable before the active clock edge

source: VisCon authored practice · not an ETH exam
explanation: Setup time concerns stability before the edge; hold time concerns stability after it.

subject: ddca
title: Finite-state-machine state bits
prompt: What is the minimum number of binary state bits needed to encode 10 distinct states?
source: VisCon authored practice · not an ETH exam
explanation: Three bits encode only 8 states; four bits encode 16.

subject: ddca
title: Byte addressing
prompt: In a byte-addressable memory, consecutive byte addresses differ by how much?
source: VisCon authored practice · not an ETH exam
explanation: Each address identifies one byte, so the next byte is at address + 1.

subject: ddca
title: Address-space size
prompt: A byte-addressable system has 16-bit addresses. How many bytes can it address?
source: VisCon authored practice · not an ETH exam
explanation: There are 2¹⁶ distinct addresses, each naming one byte.

subject: ddca
title: Little-endian storage
prompt: A 32-bit value 0x12345678 is stored in little-endian order. Which byte is at the lowest address?
source: VisCon authored practice · not an ETH exam
explanation: Little-endian layout places the least significant byte at the lowest address.

subject: ddca
title: Load/store architecture
prompt: In a classic load/store instruction-set architecture, which instructions directly transfer data between registers and memory?
source: VisCon authored practice · not an ETH exam
explanation: Arithmetic generally operates on registers; explicit loads and stores access data memory.

subject: ddca
title: The program counter
prompt: What does the program counter primarily track?

options.text: The value of the most recent arithmetic result
The size of the data cache

source: VisCon authored practice · not an ETH exam
explanation: The program counter tracks the instruction-fetch position. Exact update timing depends on the processor design.

subject: ddca
title: A register destination
prompt: A register-register instruction computes R3 ← R1 + R2. Which register receives the result?
source: VisCon authored practice · not an ETH exam
explanation: R3 is the destination named on the left side of the assignment.

subject: ddca
title: CPU execution time
prompt: A program executes 1,000 instructions with average CPI 2 on a 1 GHz processor. What is its CPU execution time?
source: VisCon authored practice · not an ETH exam
explanation: Time = instruction count × CPI / frequency = 2000 / 10⁹ seconds = 2 microseconds.

subject: ddca
title: Clock period
prompt: What is the clock period of a 2 GHz clock?
source: VisCon authored practice · not an ETH exam
explanation: The period is 1 / frequency = 1 / (2×10⁹) seconds.

subject: ddca
title: Amdahl’s law
prompt: Half of a program’s original execution time is accelerated by a factor of 2; the other half is unchanged. What is the overall speedup?
source: VisCon authored practice · not an ETH exam
explanation: The new normalized time is 0.5 + 0.5/2 = 0.75, so speedup is 1/0.75 = 4/3.

subject: ddca
title: A data dependency
prompt: Instruction I1 writes register R1; the immediately following instruction I2 reads R1. What dependency is present?
source: VisCon authored practice · not an ETH exam
explanation: I2 needs the value produced by I1. Whether a stall is needed depends on forwarding and pipeline timing.

subject: ddca
title: A structural hazard
prompt: What causes a structural hazard in a pipeline?

options.text: Two instructions use different independent resources
Two operations need the same unavailable hardware resource at the same time

source: VisCon authored practice · not an ETH exam
explanation: A structural hazard is a conflict over hardware resources.

subject: ddca
title: Ideal pipeline cycles
prompt: An ideal 5-stage pipeline starts empty and issues one instruction per cycle, with no stalls. How many cycles finish 10 instructions?
source: VisCon authored practice · not an ETH exam
explanation: The first instruction takes 5 cycles; the remaining 9 complete one per cycle: 5 + 9 = 14.

subject: ddca
title: Cache-line offset
prompt: How many byte-offset bits are needed for a 64-byte cache line in a byte-addressable system?
source: VisCon authored practice · not an ETH exam
explanation: Six bits select one of 2⁶ = 64 bytes.

subject: ddca
title: Direct-mapped sets
prompt: A direct-mapped cache stores 1 KiB of data in 64-byte lines. How many sets does it have?
source: VisCon authored practice · not an ETH exam
explanation: There are 1024 / 64 = 16 lines; a direct-mapped cache has one line per set.

subject: ddca
title: Average memory access time
prompt: A cache lookup takes 1 ns. The miss rate is 5%, and a miss adds 40 ns beyond the lookup. What is the average access time?
source: VisCon authored practice · not an ETH exam
explanation: Average time = hit/lookup time + miss rate × extra penalty = 1 + 0.05×40 = 3 ns.

subject: ddca
title: Write-back behavior
prompt: In a write-back cache, when is a modified line normally written to the next memory level?

options.text: When the dirty line is evicted or explicitly flushed

source: VisCon authored practice · not an ETH exam
explanation: A write-back cache marks a modified line dirty and defers propagation until eviction or a required flush.

subject: ddca
title: Page offset bits
prompt: With 4 KiB pages and byte addressing, how many bits form the page offset?
source: VisCon authored practice · not an ETH exam
explanation: 4 KiB = 4096 bytes = 2¹² bytes, requiring 12 offset bits.

subject: ddca
title: The TLB’s role
prompt: What does a translation lookaside buffer (TLB) cache?
source: VisCon authored practice · not an ETH exam
explanation: A TLB accelerates address translation by caching page translations and associated permissions.

subject: ddca
title: A page fault
prompt: What can cause a page fault when a process accesses virtual memory?

options.text: Every access to a different cache line
The referenced page is not currently mapped as resident and accessible

source: VisCon authored practice · not an ETH exam
explanation: A missing/nonresident page or a disallowed access can raise a page fault. A TLB miss alone may be resolved by a page-table walk.
